comparator.name: Dutch Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Dutch-language programme has 60 EC in year one, 30 EC compulsory in year two, 50 EC of restricted choices across years two and three, 30 EC open electives and a 10 EC thesis. The Dutch Linguistics internal option follows the degree’s Dutch-language focus. Two compulsory and three first-listed eligible 10 EC choices are spread across the two spring terms. The formal regulations do not identify a graduation direction. They require prerequisites shown on the individual course records and board review where minor courses duplicate degree requirements. The year-one mentoring meetings and thesis seminar are required and carry no additional EC.

Language use, argumentation, stylistics, persuasion and communication in social settings

alternatives.label: Language, persuasion, cognition & media
alternatives.labelReason: Rhetoric, stylistics and media are central alongside language processing, research methods and social influence. Beginner Dutch supports the context without replacing specialist analysis.
alternatives.concept: Study how language and arguments shape understanding through rhetoric, stylistics, psycholinguistics and media analysis. Begin learning Dutch for everyday communication and apply rhetoric through work with local schoolchildren. These courses offer different ways to study language use and persuasion.
progression: Brain and Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics and Higher Order Functions. Introductory rhetoric precedes applied persuasion and school-based practice. Beginner Dutch is placed before the school work.

alternatives.label: Literature, cultural history & media
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature, six media, four communication, three history, two art/museum and two sociology courses give the programme a predominantly literary and cultural organising logic. The two visual-art courses are complementary study of cultural representation and display, not Dutch art-history coverage.
alternatives.concept: Interpret literature across periods and cultures and study how stories change across print, film and documentary. Historical research, art and museum study provide context for interpreting texts and cultural representation.
alternatives.distinctness: 9 courses differ in each direction. Literary history, adaptation, art and historical inquiry replace specialist persuasion, applied rhetoric, and cognitive and psychological inquiry.
progression: Introductory literary and film analysis precedes advanced interpretation, adaptation and documentary work. Modern history precedes the final American history research seminar.

selection.assessment: The first option responds directly through rhetoric, stylistics, language processing and mediated communication. The second responds through a sequence in literary interpretation, comparative cultural history and media. A third structural, historical and social linguistics option lacks enough substantive courses in language structure, change and variation to form a distinct coherent direction. Existing psycholinguistics, stylistics and beginner Dutch already contribute to the first option. Digital text corpora support the external degree without establishing a separate UCR data science direction.

notes.text: Leiden develops specialist knowledge of Dutch language structure, variation and history alongside Dutch literature from the Middle Ages to the present. UCR covers related methods through rhetoric, language processing, literature and media. Its beginner Dutch course teaches everyday communication. Leiden also requires an individual thesis within the chosen subject area.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden studies the Dutch language, older and modern Dutch literature, rhetoric, and how language and literature interact with media. Students apply these methods in a supervised thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option focuses on language, persuasion and cognition. The other focuses on literature, cultural history and media. Both offer related academic methods. Leiden provides more depth in Dutch linguistics and Dutch literary history.
